<!-- pr-reviewer: ee7270eed4e0ea1fa7e7f115f55c1a10b8869514 -->
**Verdict: Needs changes before merge.** One test that is green on `main` is red on the trial merge.

This is a SAFETY-tier review. The PR changes posted G-code (new G2/G3 output for the wire posts), the wire gouge laws and the wire verifier in `camcraft-sim`.

## What looks good

- The analytic offset (`arc_offset.rs`) refuses each failure case by name: an inside arc tighter than the kerf, a consumed parallel, a neck, and parallels that do not meet. Nothing is clamped.
- Two independent checks guard the output. The motion kerf law reads the drawing exactly (`arc_laws.rs`). The sim verifier reads each arc as chords and subtracts the chord sagitta (`kerf.rs`, `arcs.rs`).
- A tabbed cut with arcs and an arc on a leaning wire are "unreadable" by name. They never pass silently.
- The exact-polygon path of #3180 stays byte for byte (`exact_polygon()`).
- I read the six new goldens against the drawings, line by line:
  - `wire_dxf_die_circle.nc` (ISO, G-EDM, Sodick): lead X6 Y5 to X10.835 Y5, then two G3 half turns of radius 4.835 about X6 Y5, then the lead-out. 4.835 = 5 - 0.165. This is correct.
  - `wire_dxf_punch_fillet.nc`: the drawing walks counter-clockwise (the shoelace sum of its corners is positive). Each of the four outside corners has a G3 pivot of radius 0.165 about the corner. The inside corner at X6 Y5 is trimmed to X5.835 Y5.165. The fillet is `G3 X13. Y15.165 I-3.165 J0.`: centre X13 Y12, radius 3 + 0.165. The lead from X6 Y25 stays outside the punch. This is correct.
- The new modules have provenance lines. The new files are under 400 lines. Clippy is clean.

## Results, merged with main (locally, macOS)

Trial merge: PR head `ee7270eed` + upstream/main `02d05bc1c`. The merge is clean.

| Step | Result |
|---|---|
| `motion build`, `motion suites: lib`, `motion suites: wire_fans` | ok |
| `sim suites: lib` | ok |
| `post build` + 49 `post suites` (all `script_*` posts, `recorded_streams`, `agie_inspection`) | ok |
| `app build (--no-run)`, `app suites: lib` | ok |
| `cl suites: headless_bin` | ok |
| `app suites`: all 17 `wire_*` suites, `wire_dxf_selection`, `g_edm_post`, 4 `sodick_*`, `edm_*`, `verify`, `verify_arc_reading`, `golden_cl`, `recorded_post_streams`, `posting`, `project_roundtrip`, `commands_undo`, `mcp_wire_contour`, `mcp_dxf`, `feature_pick_wire`, 4 `contour_dxf_*`, `slot_dxf_sketch`, `sketch_profile` | ok |
| `app suites: example_catalog`, `example_catalog_adaptive`, `example_catalog_edge_work` | ok |
| **`app suites: agie_native`** | **FAIL** (35 passed, 1 failed) |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |

The failing test, on the trial merge (it fails again when run alone):

```
---- tangent::a_short_inner_offgrid_edge_or_folded_loop_publishes_nothing stdout ----
panicked at crates/app/tests/agie_native/tangent.rs:99:9:
convex loop: ... generation refused: invalid machining parameters: wire contour: the start hole at X0.000 Y-21.000 lies inside the profile - a punch is cut from outside it; the wire would burn through the punch
```

The same test on bare upstream/main `02d05bc1c` (same worktree, same build): **ok**. Main did not change any wire, Agie or post code after the PR base `b13ebd440`. Thus this PR causes the failure.

Not run: the quick plan also names about 600 other `app` suites. The plan names them only because they share `tests/golden/nc/` as test input, or the `app::operation` gate map. I did not run them, because the verdict is already "needs changes". The light lane did not run.

**Extra suites run** (user selection): no file under `testdata/` changed, and no importer code changed. Thus no extra suites apply.

## Mutations (safety tier)

1. Pivot arc radius `k` changed to `0.9 * k` in `arc_offset.rs`:
   - `motion suites: lib` is red: `line_and_arc_die_trims_outside_corners_and_pivots_the_reentrant_one`, `line_and_arc_punch_pivots_outside_corners_and_trims_the_inside_corner`;
   - `wire_dxf_selection` is red: `arcs::line_and_arc_punch_pivots_its_corners_and_posts_its_goldens`.
2. The kerf offset moved 2 um into the product (`k - 0.002` in `arc_cut.rs`), and the motion kerf law disabled (`arc_laws::kerf` returns `Ok` at once). Thus only the sim verifier can see the gouge. `wire_dxf_selection` is red at `arcs.rs:63`: the verifier gives `Gouge { depth: 0.002 }` for the die circle and for the punch.

Both mutations are reverted. The tree is clean.

## Requested before merge

1. **`crates/app/tests/agie_native/tangent.rs:90-94` is red because of this PR.** The PR body says that `agie_native` is ok, but on this head it fails.
   - Cause: `run_job_arms` (`crates/app/src/operation/generate.rs:211-217`) now sends each selected chain that is not an exact polygon to `generate_arcs` first, also for the Agie machine. Before, `nominal_ring` sent a punch to `WireProfile`, which refused a loop that is not convex and tangent ("convex loop").
   - The case with the arc from 180 to 360 degrees makes a lower half circle down to Y-29. This shape encloses the start hole X0 Y-21. Thus the new refusal "lies inside the profile" is geometrically correct. The program is still refused, and nothing is published. The defect is the stale test, not unsafe output.
   - Fix: update the test to the new route and keep its intent. For example, move the start hole of that case out of the half circle, so that the native door still gives "convex loop". Or assert the new refusal text for that case. Then record the change of refusal order for the Agie machine in `docs/decisions/3937-wire-dxf-arcs.md`.
   - Class: the PR changes which door refuses first for a selected Agie chain. Please run the whole `agie_native` suite (`cargo xtask gate quick --only "app suites: agie_native"`) and each other suite that asserts a refusal text of a selected-chain door. Then name the result in the PR body.

## Notes (not blocking)

- `crates/app/src/operation/generate.rs` was 4,606 lines and is now 4,617 lines. It was already over the 400-line limit. This PR does not cause that.
- The verifier gives the gouge of mutation 2 at `move_no: 1` (the lead-in end), not at an arc move. This is correct, because the lead ends on the path. But a move number on the arc would help the user more. This is a possible follow-up (P7).
- Heavy step: the PR body says that no `#[ignore]` heavy test covers `motion::wire_edm` or `sim::verify::wire`. I agree, from the dry run. Thus no targeted heavy step applies.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

This PR is a draft again. The quick gate result in the body was wrong: the log that I read came from an earlier run on a different branch. The real quick gate on `ee7270eed` did not complete. I now run the quick gate again on this head. I will update the body with the real result, and then flag the PR ready again.
